moves.move_text_short: Set up parameterized NLS family on metric graph; isolate Morse-index-bounded, lambda_n -> infty regime
moves.why_not: This is regime selection / problem scoping; no v5 op covers 'declare the asymptotic regime under which subsequent analysis runs'; broad_05's constraints progressively narrow to a unique form, whereas these constraints just delimit a study window.

moves.move_text_short: Adapt Morse-index definition to metric graphs by replacing test-function space C_c^infty with H^1 cap C_c
moves.why: A foundational definition (Morse index) is structurally broadened by enlarging the admissible test-function class so the concept covers a new class of phenomena (vertices, Kirchhoff conditions); this is exactly the 'broaden definitions to encompass more phenomena' mechanism, identical in inferential shape to v3's tb_01/tb_09 collapsed into core_07.

moves.move_text_short: Liouville rigidity on star graph for sign-changing solutions via oscillation + disjoint test functions
moves.why_not: This is theorem-proof craft (Liouville-type rigidity via nodal-piece test functions); core_07 is about redefining concepts not generalizing theorems, and core_05 extremal-case requires an extremal object whose extremality forces rigidity (no minimal counterexample is invoked here).

moves.move_text_short: Develop graph-native maximum principle (weak + strong) handling vertex condition via derivative sums
moves.why_not: Re-deriving an analogue of a classical PDE theorem in a new setting is not 'broadening a definition' (core_07's mechanism) and not black-box import (core_06); it is in-setting estimate craft, which the v5 vocabulary does not capture.

moves.move_text_short: Construct explicit cosh comparison function on bounded interval as reusable exponential majorant
moves.why_not: Barrier-function construction is canonical PDE estimate craft with no structural analog among the 18 ops (no op describes 'build an explicit pointwise majorant').

moves.move_text_short: ODE convexity dichotomy: local max of |u| either >= fixed height or u vanishes on incident edges
moves.why_not: A quantitative dichotomy produced by an ODE convexity argument is local PDE craft; no v5 op describes 'derive a height-or-vanish alternative'.

moves.move_text_short: Split blow-up analysis into two cases: maxima away from vertices vs accumulating at vertex
moves.why_not: This is a case split that anticipates two distinct limit problems; core_03 Canonical Decomposition requires partitioning into well-understood components glued back into a global property, which does not happen here (the cases are alternative scenarios, not glued pieces).

moves.move_text_short: Rescaling u_n at candidate blow-up point and passing to limit profile via compactness
moves.why_not: Concentration-compactness rescaling is a domain-specific PDE move; core_01 requires an equivalence between formal systems where theorems transport, but the limit problem is an asymptotic profile rather than an equivalent reformulation of the original.

moves.move_text_short: Transfer spectral data (positive frequency, Morse-index bounds) from prelimit to limit profile
moves.why_not: Inheriting properties through a weak limit is not iterative refinement (core_02), not local-to-global gluing (core_04), and not bootstrapping a weak property to a strong one via self-reference (broad_06).

moves.move_text_short: Iterative selection of well-separated blow-up points until residual mass is exhausted
moves.why_not: Greedy enumeration of distinct peaks does not match core_02's mechanism of repeatedly improving the quality metric of a single candidate toward a fixed point; here each iteration produces a new object, not a refinement of one.

moves.move_text_short: Cap blow-up-point count by Morse index via disjoint test functions giving independent negative directions
moves.why_not: Pigeonhole-by-dimension contradiction with the Morse-index hypothesis is not extremal-case analysis (core_05 needs an extremal object whose extremality forces rigidity); it is a counting-via-quadratic-form argument the vocabulary does not encode.

moves.move_text_short: Glue local cosh / exponential barriers at vertices into a graph-wide barrier giving global exponential decay
moves.why: Local exponential-decay barriers are proved on each edge / near each blow-up point and then assembled via a vertex-transmission gluing argument into a global decay estimate across the whole graph; this is exactly the local-patches-plus-consistency-gluing-to-global mechanism of core_04.

moves.move_text_short: Subdivide edges by inserting auxiliary degree-2 vertices where distance function changes expression
moves.why_not: This is a substrate refinement (re-meshing the graph) to make a particular barrier lemma applicable; no v5 op describes 'refine the underlying combinatorial substrate so a tool applies piecewise'.

moves.move_text_short: Convert global exponential decay into integral asymptotic for lambda^alpha integral |u|^q
moves.why_not: This is computing an asymptotic limit by absorbing exterior contributions; broad_04 Bounding via Surrogate replaces an exact quantity with a tractable bound, whereas here the exact integral is shown to converge to a determined limit, not bounded by a surrogate.

moves.move_text_short: Extract uniform L^2-prescribed bound on lambda_n when p != 6 as corollary of (1.5)
moves.why_not: Direct corollary extraction from a previously proved estimate is not a structural move in the v5 sense; nothing about it matches the eighteen mechanisms.

moves.move_text_short: Four-star example showing m can differ from number of local maxima; discrepancy hidden in limit profile
moves.why_not: An illustrative counterexample to a naive expectation is not an extremal-case-forcing-rigidity move (core_05) and not a systematic catalog (broad_07); it is a single demonstrative example.

moves.move_text_short: Pivot to a priori bounds; relate four invariants (nodal zones, Morse index, L^infty, L^2); flag where inequalities fail
moves.why_not: Setting up a relational map among invariants and recording failure cases is structural-program declaration; no v5 op encodes 'enumerate invariant relationships and counterexamples to each direction'.

moves.move_text_short: Adapt Bahri-Lions Morse-index lower bound by nodal zones to graphs, with care for zero set of rho
moves.why_not: The Bahri-Lions argument is re-derived with modifications for the rho-vanishing case rather than treated as a black-box module with verified preconditions, so core_06 does not apply; and no definition is broadened, so core_07 does not apply.

moves.move_text_short: Separate compact-case (eigenvalue) and half-line-case (W-infimum) lower bounds on lambda by Morse index
moves.why_not: Two parallel theorems indexed by underlying geometry are a case split, not canonical decomposition (no gluing of components into a global property) and not extremal-case analysis.

moves.move_text_short: Apply Hartman ODE superlinear bound on each edge to get per-edge L^infty bound on graphs
moves.why: A classical ODE result of Hartman is invoked as a black-box module on each one-dimensional edge with the precondition (one-dimensional superlinear ODE) explicitly verified, yielding the L^infty bound; this is the canonical 'import major theorem, verify preconditions, use as module' mechanism of core_06.

moves.move_text_short: Establish converse (L^infty bound forces Morse-index bound) on compact / localized settings; counterexamples on tadpole, Z-periodic
moves.why_not: Proving a converse and exhibiting failure on noncompact graphs is not characterization-by-exclusion (sub_01_graph excludes minors / forbidden substructures from an object class), and not systematic cataloging.

moves.move_text_short: Matching upper/lower L^2 bounds in lambda from (1.5); three settings (compact, localized, half-line) for small lambda
moves.why_not: Three parallel theorems indexed by graph geometry is a setting-by-setting case analysis; broad_07 Systematic Cataloging classifies an object class by canonical types with coverage verification, but there is no claim of exhaustive type coverage here, just three named common settings.

moves.move_text_short: Sharpness of lambda^{-1/4} via tadpole construction: implicit-function family at periodic-solution backbone
moves.why_not: Sharpness-by-explicit-construction is bespoke PDE / ODE craft; no v5 op describes 'build a parametric family by implicit-function continuation off a known periodic solution to saturate a rate'.

moves.move_text_short: Appendix records conserved energy and existence of sign-changing periodic solutions of underlying NLS ODE
moves.why_not: Packaging foundational ODE facts in an appendix is bookkeeping for downstream use; no v5 op encodes 'isolate prerequisite one-dimensional facts the constructions rely on'.
